newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Senate passes dole bill without changes.
newsitem.headline: Australia Senate passes dole bill without changes.

text.p: The Australian government's controversial work-for-the-dole scheme passed through parliament unscathed on Tuesday, ending the government's threat of an early election on the unemployment issue.
"It went through the senate and there's no amendments at all," a spokesman for Training Minister David Kemp told Reuters.
The spokesman said the first work-for-the-dole projects in the A$15 million scheme would start in October.
The legislation passed the non-government dominated upper house of parliament, the Senate, after the opposition withdrew its support for an amendment to end the scheme after a two-year trial period.
It was the second time the legislation has gone before the Senate after the lower house of parliament, the House of Representatives, voted against the sunset clause amendment on Monday night.
The Labor opposition had supported the amendment when the bill first appeared in the Senate.
The government, which needs two additional votes to pass any legislation in the Senate, had threatened an early election if the work-for-the-dole bill was changed in any way.
Under the Australian constitution, both houses of parliament can be dissolved and an early election called if the Senate twice rejects government legislation after more than three months.

The work-for-the-dole legislation, under which some young people would be made to work for unemployment benefits, was one of three items over which the government has threatened an early election. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
